about: Source-linked therapeutic platform explorer. Platform class is defined by the administered preparation (live, killed intact whole-cell, isolated cell-wall material, or extracted/derived component), not merely by species. Product-specific clinical evidence and status do not transfer across preparations.

entries.name: Mycobacterium bovis BCG
entries.mechanism: Local BCG exposure can recruit innate immune cells and support antitumor immune responses in the bladder; the precise mechanisms are multifactorial.
entries.cargo: No engineered payload in the licensed TICE BCG product.
entries.evidence: Licensed bacterial therapeutic for specified non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer indications; not a precedent proving engineered platforms.
entries.notes: Specific BCG strains and products are not interchangeable without evidence.

entries.name: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium
entries.mechanism: Tumor-associated exposure, bacterial sensing, and local inflammatory activation have been investigated with attenuated strains; broad clinical antitumor efficacy is unproven.
entries.cargo: Investigational surface/payload engineering; strain-specific, not a single validated cargo.
entries.delivery: Systemic or local in historic clinical studies; research only.
entries.evidence: Human phase 1 experience exists for VNP20009; not an approved cancer treatment.

sources.label: Phase I study of attenuated Salmonella VNP20009

entries.notes: VNP20009 is a historical experimental strain. Other attenuated Salmonella platforms (including MUL001) are separate programs; evidence from one strain should not be transferred to another.

entries.name: Listeria monocytogenes
entries.mechanism: Attenuated platforms are studied to stimulate antigen-specific T-cell immunity using intracellular antigen handling.
entries.cargo: Cancer-antigen cargo in investigational platforms.
entries.evidence: Cancer-vaccine studies have involved attenuated strains; no general approval for Listeria as cancer therapy.

sources.label: Listeria vaccine vectors and therapeutic immune responses
Attenuated Listeria platform for cancer immunotherapy

entries.name: Clostridium novyi
entries.mechanism: Tumor hypoxia-associated growth and local lysis/inflammation were studied in a first-in-human intratumoral study.
entries.cargo: No specific engineered therapeutic cargo in the cited NT study.
entries.evidence: A Phase 1 study reported biologic activity and clinically important adverse events; not an approved treatment.

entries.name: Escherichia coli
entries.mechanism: EcN is a widely studied chassis for engineered substrate conversion, biological sensing, and local expression of therapeutic functions; mechanisms depend on the construct.
entries.cargo: Examples include metabolite-conversion enzymes or therapeutic proteins in distinct programs.
entries.delivery: Typically oral for gut-targeted programs; alternative routes are experimental.
entries.evidence: Clinical research includes historical Synlogic engineered EcN programs; their outcomes and status are program-specific.

sources.label: FDA orphan designation: engineered E. coli Nissle 1917
Clinical study planning for Synlogic SYNB1934

entries.name: Escherichia coli
entries.strain: Attenuated, killed and stabilized non-pathogenic E. coli; Indaptus Decoy10 / Decoy20
components: Intact killed E. coli bacterial cells
entries.mechanism: Killed, stabilized E. coli preparations were designed to engage multiple innate immune receptors, including TLR2, TLR4, TLR8, TLR9, NOD2 and STING, to induce immune activation; this does not establish clinical efficacy.
entries.cargo: Native bacterial immunostimulatory components; not a living bacterial delivery chassis.
entries.delivery: Intravenous investigational administration; not an approved therapy.
entries.evidence: Peer-reviewed preclinical/mechanistic work and Phase 1 investigation of Decoy20. Company disclosures in 2026 reported discontinuation of further Decoy20 clinical development.
entries.notes: Nonliving whole-cell E. coli is distinct from live/engineered E. coli Nissle 1917. Decoy10 and Decoy20 are investigational formulations, not approved products.

entries.name: Lactococcus lactis
entries.mechanism: Engineered bacteria have been studied for local IL-10 exposure and mucosal immune regulation in Crohn's disease.
entries.cargo: IL-10 in the historical LL-Thy12 research program.
entries.evidence: Phase 1 feasibility research was published; this is not an approved Crohn's therapy.

sources.label: Phase I engineered Lactococcus lactis expressing IL-10

entries.name: Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris / L. cremoris
entries.mechanism: The engineered lactic-acid bacterial chassis is being investigated for delivery of therapeutic protein functions in tumor-related research.
entries.cargo: Engineered therapeutic proteins; exact program-dependent functions should be checked against public disclosure.
entries.delivery: Program-specific investigational delivery; not an approved route.
entries.evidence: Company reports AUP-55 as preclinical; results from a separate wound-healing program cannot establish its oncology efficacy.

entries.name: Clostridium butyricum
entries.modality: Live probiotic adjunct in immunotherapy studies
entries.mechanism: CBM588 has been investigated as an oral adjunct to immune-checkpoint therapy, potentially affecting gut microbial composition and immune response.
entries.cargo: Native metabolic activity, not an engineered oncology payload.
entries.evidence: Small randomized clinical studies exist; these do not establish a universally effective cancer therapy.

entries.name: Akkermansia muciniphila
entries.strain: Live Akkermansia muciniphila; human feasibility research
entries.modality: Live commensal preparation (distinct from pasteurized product)
entries.mechanism: Mucin-associated ecology, host barrier interactions and immunometabolic signaling are under active investigation, including pasteurized preparations.
entries.cargo: Native surface proteins and metabolites; no engineered cargo in cited trials.
entries.evidence: Human trials have examined safety and metabolic outcomes; clinical effects are preparation- and indication-dependent.

sources.label: Pasteurized A. muciniphila weight-loss maintenance trial (2026)

entries.notes: Live and pasteurized experimental formulations are catalogued separately in this explorer.

entries.name: Akkermansia muciniphila
entries.strain: Pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila MucT; nonviable whole-cell preparation
entries.stage: Human proof-of-concept and randomized clinical research
entries.mechanism: Pasteurized, nonviable A. muciniphila has been investigated for metabolic effects, including effects potentially associated with its bacterial surface molecules. Clinical findings are formulation- and population-specific.
entries.cargo: Native surface proteins and metabolites; no engineered cargo in cited trials.
entries.evidence: Human proof-of-concept work compared live and pasteurized preparations; a 2026 randomized clinical study investigated pasteurized A. muciniphila in weight-loss maintenance.
entries.notes: Pasteurization makes this a nonliving whole-cell preparation, not a cell-wall extract or a live probiotic.

entries.name: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii
entries.mechanism: A butyrate-producing intestinal commensal studied for immune regulation and intestinal epithelial interactions; Gram-staining and envelope classification require nuance.
entries.cargo: Native microbial metabolic functions, not an engineered payload in the referenced EXL01 study.
entries.evidence: A first-in-human Crohn's disease study was published in 2026; not an approved treatment.

sources.label: Ecology and atypical envelope of F. prausnitzii

entries.name: Bifidobacterium longum
entries.mechanism: Bifidobacterial ecology and immune interactions have been investigated as probiotic or engineered-delivery concepts.
entries.cargo: Native microbial metabolites; research concepts include strain-specific proteins.
entries.evidence: No single clinical-efficacy claim applies to all strains of B. longum.

sources.label: Search B. longum clinical evidence on PubMed

entries.name: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
entries.strain: Formerly Lactobacillus plantarum; diverse probiotic strains
entries.mechanism: Cell-envelope and metabolite effects vary across probiotic strains and experimental host settings.
entries.cargo: Native fermentation products; engineered cargo only in individual research programs.
entries.delivery: Oral probiotic and investigational mucosal studies.
entries.evidence: A species name alone cannot establish strain-specific clinical benefits.

entries.name: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus
entries.mechanism: The LGG strain is studied for mucosal adherence and immune modulation; disease-specific effect sizes and safety depend on the population and intervention.
entries.cargo: Native microbial function; not a genetically engineered therapeutic cargo.
entries.evidence: Probiotic evidence is strain-specific and does not imply cancer therapy or universal therapeutic effects.

entries.name: Bacillus subtilis
entries.strain: Selected probiotic strains; research-stage engineered platforms
entries.mechanism: Spore tolerance and bacterial surface architecture motivate strain-specific probiotic and delivery research, without implying approved engineered biologics.
entries.cargo: Experimental antigen or protein display concepts only.
entries.evidence: Clinical outcomes and quality attributes are strain- and product-dependent.

sources.label: Search B. subtilis probiotic clinical trials

entries.name: Alkalihalobacillus clausii (Bacillus clausii)
entries.mechanism: Spore survival and effects on community function have been investigated in gastrointestinal probiotic settings; mechanisms differ by strain.
entries.cargo: Native bacterial functions; no general engineered-cargo program established.
entries.evidence: Not equivalent to a licensed treatment for systemic inflammatory or oncologic disease.

entries.name: Bacteroides fragilis
entries.mechanism: Capsular polysaccharide A has been studied for host immune regulation in experimental systems. Strain variation and pathogenic potential matter.
entries.cargo: Native polysaccharides; not an approved therapeutic bacterial product.
entries.evidence: Do not generalize from non-toxigenic research strains to pathogenic or enterotoxigenic strains.

sources.label: Bacteroides fragilis polysaccharide A immunoregulation review search

entries.name: Defined bacterial-spore community
entries.stage: FDA approved for recurrent CDI prevention
indications: Prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection following antibiotic treatment
entries.mechanism: Defined administration of a bacterial-spore community aims to restore colonization resistance after microbiome disruption.
entries.cargo: Community composition; not a single engineered bacterial strain.
entries.evidence: FDA approved for prevention of recurrent CDI in qualifying adults; not approved to treat active CDI or unrelated diseases.
entries.notes: A community product is not a single named bacterial species.

entries.name: Microbiota community therapy
entries.stage: FDA approved for recurrent CDI prevention
indications: Prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection after antibiotic treatment
entries.mechanism: Microbiota restoration and ecological competition are proposed contributors to reduced recurrence risk.
entries.cargo: Live donor-derived bacterial microbiota, not a single engineered strain.
entries.evidence: FDA approved for prevention of recurrent CDI in qualifying adults; not approved for oncology or cardiometabolic disease.
entries.notes: Contains multiple bacterial taxa; it is not a species-level product.

entries.name: Nocardia rubra
entries.stage: Clinical observational and translational research; indication-specific
entries.mechanism: Studies report modulation of dendritic cells and macrophages and local immune pathways; evidence does not establish efficacy for all cancer indications.
entries.cargo: No living bacteria or engineered cargo; cell-wall material is the investigated intervention.
entries.delivery: Local external administration in cited cervical studies; route varies by research context.
entries.evidence: Human cervical immune-marker studies and mechanistic cancer research are available; no blanket FDA oncology approval is implied.
entries.notes: Cell-wall skeleton preparations are distinct from intact killed bacteria.

entries.name: Multi-species bacterial lysate
entries.strain: OM-85: lysate derived from multiple bacterial strains
entries.modality: Nonliving bacterial lysate / mixed bacterial extracts
entries.stage: Human clinical research; regulatory status varies by country and indication
entries.mechanism: Bacterial lysates are investigated for immune modulation at mucosal and systemic sites; efficacy varies by population, formulation and endpoint.
entries.cargo: Bacterial extract, not intact killed cells, isolated cell-wall skeletons, or live organisms.
entries.delivery: Oral bacterial lysate preparations studied in respiratory indications.
entries.evidence: Clinical studies and systematic reviews report heterogeneous benefits and limitations. Do not infer approval or recommendation in every jurisdiction.

sources.label: OM-85 clinical evidence and consensus review

entries.notes: This is a representative lysate preparation; it is not an isolated bacterial species.
